solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: How Donald talks about not roaming the hills (9)

indicatorNotes.about: Talking about something puts it in the middle of the talk, so QUACKS is wrapped round the other piece.
indicatorNotes.roaming: Letters that go roaming wander from their places, so NOT comes back in a new order.

annotation.surface: A duck grumbling about being kept off the hills.
annotation.walkthrough: The Quantocks are a range of hills in Somerset, England. 'Donald' is Donald Duck, whose talk is all quacking.
annotation.definitionFit: A proper name for a particular range: the Quantock Hills in Somerset are called the Quantocks for short.

entries.clue: Land in Iraq, at Ar-Rutbah (5)

indicatorNotes.in: What is in the following words is contained by them, so the answer runs inside the letters of 'Iraq, at Ar-Rutbah'.

annotation.surface: Directions to a plot of land in a western Iraqi town.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is so Middle Eastern that a solver hunts for a region of Iraq; the neighbouring Gulf state is lying across the word breaks.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Qatar is a country, and a country is a land.

entries.clue: Like even an exam (2-5)

annotation.surface: Something described as being as flat as an exam.
annotation.walkthrough: An AS-level is an English school exam, the first half of a full A-level, taken at about 17.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the AS-level is one particular exam in the English school system.

entries.clue: Listing of forbidden language about love (10)

indicatorNotes.about: About means around, so the language is placed around the love.

annotation.surface: A catalogue of banned words about love, as a censor might keep.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Forbidden language' reads as one idea, swear words; it is two pieces, and the forbidden piece takes the older spelling of taboo.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a tabulation sets items out in a table, which is a kind of listing.

entries.clue: In burial site, weep and part (5)

blocks.note: PT is the standard abbreviation for part

annotation.surface: A mourner weeping at a graveside before going their separate way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Part' is a verb in the surface, taking leave; here it is the noun, abbreviated.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a crypt is the vault beneath a church where the dead were laid.

entries.clue: Helped to be made a fool of on the radio (9)

indicatorNotes.on the radio: Radio is heard rather than read, so the answer only has to sound like the words it comes from.

blocks.note: to be suckered is to be made a fool of

annotation.surface: Someone helped into being mocked live on a radio show.
annotation.walkthrough: In a British accent, with the R silent, the two words are said the same way.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense: to succour someone is to give them help in need.

entries.clue: Tall building with many owners apart from English (5)

indicatorNotes.apart from: Everything apart from the E is kept, so that one letter is dropped from the word.

annotation.surface: A tower block in multiple ownership, none of the owners English.
annotation.walkthrough: The Shard is the tallest building in London, a glass spire by London Bridge.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Shard is one particular skyscraper in London.

entries.clue: Over-sleeps allotted time (4)

indicatorNotes.Over: To turn something over is to flip it, so the word that follows is written backwards.

annotation.surface: Someone who oversleeps and eats into the time they were given.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over-sleeps' looks like one word; the hyphen splits off the indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a span is a stretch of time, as in the life span one is allotted.

entries.clue: Draw a sort of racing driver group together at the start (7)

indicatorNotes.at the start: Only what stands at the start of 'together' is used, its first letter.

blocks.note: the TT (Tourist Trophy) is the Isle of Man motorbike race
the RAC (Royal Automobile Club) is a British motorists' organisation

annotation.surface: An instruction to sketch a gathering of racing drivers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Draw' as a picture word keeps the solver thinking of sketches, not of pulling in.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to draw a crowd is to attract it, pulling it towards you.

entries.clue: Irish town briefly supporting year-end event (9)

indicatorNotes.briefly: Said briefly, the town's name is cut short, losing its last letter.
indicatorNotes.supporting: In a down answer a supporter holds something up from below, so the town goes underneath.

blocks.note: ATHLONE, a town in the Irish midlands, without its E

annotation.surface: An Irish town sponsoring a New Year's Eve party.
annotation.walkthrough: The event is athletic, not a festivity: 'year-end event' is not one phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the decathlon is one particular athletics event, ten contests in two days.

entries.clue: Where big lad can store his clothes? (7)

annotation.definition: Where big lad can store his clothes?

blocks.note: read as asking about a large boy's room, and meant as the name of a thing: an adjective for big plus a word for lad
read as his wardrobe arrangements, and meant as a description of a piece of bedroom furniture with drawers

annotation.surface: Wondering where a large boy keeps his wardrobe.
annotation.walkthrough: A tallboy is a tall chest of drawers; read literally, it is a big lad, so it is where a 'tall boy' stores his clothes.
annotation.definitionFit: A tallboy is a high chest of drawers, furniture made for storing clothes, and its name also describes a big lad.

entries.clue: Confused chapter about the ear holding answer (7)

indicatorNotes.holding: Something holding another has it in its grasp, so the joined pieces keep the A inside them.

blocks.note: otic means relating to the ear

annotation.surface: A muddled section of a medical book about the ear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About the ear' is one piece, an adjective, not a container instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a chaotic scene is one in total confusion.

entries.clue: Priest takes delight in this book of his (10)

annotation.surface: A clergyman's favourite book of the Bible.
annotation.walkthrough: 'This book of his' points to the Bible, a priest's book; Revelation is its last book.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Revelation is one book of the Bible, the book a priest works from.

entries.clue: Limitless tax crushes son (4)

indicatorNotes.crushes: Something that crushes another closes in on it from all sides, so the tax surrounds the son.

annotation.surface: A son overwhelmed by an unlimited tax bill.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Limitless' reads as describing the tax; it is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: something vast is so large it seems to have no limits.

entries.clue: Stupid jeer ruined witticism (3,7)

indicatorNotes.ruined: Something ruined is wrecked, and the letters are rebuilt from the wreckage in a new order.

annotation.surface: A dumb heckle spoiling someone's clever joke.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stupid' looks like the anagram indicator; it is fodder, and 'ruined' does the work.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowing from French: a jeu d'esprit, literally a game of the mind, is a light witty remark.

entries.clue: Guide I needed through storyline (5)

indicatorNotes.needed through: What is needed through a thing runs through its middle, so I is threaded into the storyline.

annotation.surface: A writer admitting they need help finding their way through a plot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Guide' could be a verb or noun in the surface; the answer works as either.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a pilot guides ships into harbour, and to pilot is to guide.

entries.clue: Where one may find today’s crossword, or a collection of previous ones? (9)

annotation.definition: Where one may find today’s crossword

blocks.clueFragment: Where one may find today’s crossword
blocks.note: two words run together: the newspaper, and the part of it where the Times puzzle is printed, its last page
a soft-covered book of old puzzles, as sold in bookshops

annotation.surface: A question about where to find the day's crossword.
annotation.walkthrough: The first sense only works split in two: paper, then back.
annotation.definitionFit: The crossword runs on the back of the paper, and old puzzles are sold collected in paperback books.

entries.clue: In great pain I left plant (9)

annotation.surface: Someone in agony abandoning a plant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' is the verb in the surface; here it is the abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: tormentil is one particular plant, a small yellow-flowered herb of the rose family.

entries.clue: Wrongly understood cut as another cut (9)

indicatorNotes.Wrongly: Something done wrongly is out of order, so the letters are rearranged.
indicatorNotes.cut: A word that is cut is trimmed, here losing its final letter.

blocks.note: UNDERSTOOD, with the final D cut

annotation.surface: Someone misunderstanding a cut of meat as another.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut' appears twice: first as the trimming instruction, then in 'another cut', a cut of beef.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: tournedos is one particular cut of beef, a small round steak from the fillet.

entries.clue: Put an end to villain’s parting urge (9)

indicatorNotes.parting: To part something is to separate it, so the villain pushes into PROD and splits it.

annotation.surface: A scoundrel's last-minute urge before leaving.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Villain's' is 'villain is': the rogue is doing the parting.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal term: a parliament that is prorogued has its session brought to an end without being dissolved.

entries.clue: The side of the head (7)

blocks.note: read as part of the skull, and meant as a face of a coin
read as anatomy, and meant as the monarch's head, as in heads or tails

annotation.surface: A plain anatomical label: the side of someone's head.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'head' is on a coin, and heads is the obverse.
annotation.definitionFit: The obverse is the face of a coin bearing the principal design, usually a head, so it is the side of the head.

entries.clue: Exhausted as horrid noise almost doubled (3,2)

indicatorNotes.almost: Almost the whole word means all but its last letter.
indicatorNotes.doubled: Something doubled is written twice, so the noise appears two times.

blocks.note: din = horrid noise, the second copy

annotation.surface: Worn out by a racket that was nearly twice as loud.
annotation.walkthrough: Did in is British informal for wore out.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to do someone in is to wear them out, so did in means exhausted as a past-tense verb.
annotation.definitionNote: exhausted as a verb, the past tense of did in

entries.clue: Feature of kitchen artist captured in café (7)

indicatorNotes.captured in: Something captured in a place is held inside it, so the artist is shut up in the café.

annotation.surface: An artist caught on camera in a café's kitchen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Captured' suggests a picture by the artist; it only means held inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a drainer, the rack beside the sink, is one fitting of a kitchen.

entries.clue: For party it’s serious when leader is deposed (4)

indicatorNotes.when leader is deposed: A deposed leader is thrown out of first place, so the word loses its first letter.

annotation.surface: A political party in crisis once its leader is ousted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Party' and 'leader deposed' paint politics; the party here is for dancing.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a rave is one kind of party, a large all-night dance.

entries.clue: Get to sit down too long? (10)

blocks.note: get as in 'I get it', to grasp a meaning
sitting too long means not standing enough: a prefix for too little, then the verb for getting on your feet

annotation.surface: Advice on catching sitting too long.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second sense as whimsical: under- as in underfed.
annotation.definitionFit: Get means understand in plain speech, and under-stand read literally means stand too little.

entries.clue: Cross, once raves about potential reformer (2-3)

indicatorNotes.raves about: Someone who raves about is thrashing wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order.

annotation.surface: An angry person ranting about someone who might reform.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Once' tempts as EX; it is fodder, and the X comes from 'Cross'.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful description: a former prisoner is someone who may have reformed, or may yet.

entries.clue: The retreat from Moscow? (5)

blocks.note: read as an army falling back, and meant as a quiet place to get away to
read as Napoleon's route home in 1812, and meant as where Muscovites go at weekends

annotation.surface: Napoleon's army falling back from Moscow in 1812.
annotation.walkthrough: The phrase recalls Napoleon's retreat, a famous military disaster; the question mark admits the switch.
annotation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian country cottage, the place a city dweller retreats to from Moscow.

entries.clue: Kitty adjudged to have nothing missing (4)

indicatorNotes.missing: Having the nothing missing means the O is absent, so it comes out of the word.

annotation.surface: A cat judged to have nothing wrong with it.
annotation.walkthrough: Kitty looks like a cat; it is a pool of money.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a kitty is a pool of money collected for a shared purpose.

entries.clue: Stuck in the past with a different circle (7)

indicatorNotes.with a different: With a different one in its place means a swap: one circle is exchanged for another.

blocks.note: ago = in the past; its O is the circle replaced

annotation.surface: Someone stuck in the past who moved to a new social set.
annotation.walkthrough: The letter O is itself a circle, which is what lets the setter swap it for another.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a ship that runs aground is stuck fast on the bottom.

entries.clue: Very bad style worn by Ron (7)

indicatorNotes.worn by: Something worn by Ron goes round him like clothing, so the style wraps his name.

annotation.surface: A fashion verdict on Ron's terrible outfit.
annotation.walkthrough: Chronic for very bad is British slang, as in 'the service was chronic'.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: in informal British speech, chronic means very bad, beyond its medical sense of long-lasting.

entries.clue: Manipulate requirement that’s voiced (5)

indicatorNotes.that’s voiced: A word that is voiced is spoken aloud, so the answer only has to sound like it.

annotation.surface: A demand spoken aloud to control someone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Manipulate' suggests scheming; the sense is literal, working with the hands.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal sense: to knead dough or muscles is to manipulate them with the hands.

entries.clue: Crazy rations with AA health farms (9)

indicatorNotes.Crazy: Something crazy is out of its right order, so the letters are scrambled.

blocks.note: as written, joined to the fodder

annotation.surface: Wild diet rules at a health spa run like Alcoholics Anonymous.
annotation.walkthrough: 'AA' looks like the Automobile Association or Alcoholics Anonymous; it is just two letters of fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: sanatoria, the plural of sanatorium, are places where people go to recover their health.
